name: Mbere-Mbamba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Okoudowa, Bruno 2005 (fonologia) & 2010 Morfologia verbal do Lembaama, USP theses — both READ (teses.usp.br): two-tone analysis only, diacritics denote tone; no word-stress statement present. Biton 1969 and Adam 1954 sketches unreachable.

new_statements.quote: Lembaama, como muitas outras línguas do grupo banto, tem um sistema tonal de dois tons: um tom baixo [ ` ] e um tom alto [ ´ ]. [...] Os dois tons desta língua são pontuais, isto é, mantêm a mesma altura, no início ao fim de sua emissão. O tom tem uma função lexical: distingue os lexemas (verbos, nomes, numerais, etc). Na combinação dos tons, quando dois tons se encontram na fronteira entre palavras, o primeiro se apaga.
new_statements.translation: Lembaama, like many other languages of the Bantu group, has a tonal system of two tones: a low tone [ ` ] and a high tone [ ´ ]. [...] The two tones of this language are level, i.e. they keep the same pitch from the beginning to the end of their realization. Tone has a lexical function: it distinguishes lexemes (verbs, nouns, numerals, etc.). In tone combination, when two tones meet at a word boundary, the first is deleted.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible primary descriptions (Okoudowa 2005, 2010, Lembaama of Okondja) analyse the language as a two-tone (H/L) lexical tone language with no contour tones; they say nothing at all about word stress, accent or prominence, so no stress rule can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement). Tone: word-boundary tone deletion rule; nouns show more tone patterns than infinitive verbs; polysyllabic verbs prefer L.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described on citation-form nouns and infinitive verbs (word level) with a phrase-boundary tone rule; the 2010 thesis marks only H tone in running examples. No word-stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: The only accessible descriptions (Okoudowa 2005, 2010; Blanchon & Alihanga 1992) are of Lembaama/Mbaama (Obamba, Guthrie B62), spoken at Okondja and Franceville, Haut-Ogooué, Gabon (Okoudowa's own village Entogho/Otala near Okondja; Blanchon & Alihanga describe the Lempiini dialect of Eyuga = Glottolog dialect ampi1238 'Ampiini'), not Mbere proper (B61, Congo; Ndouli 2001 'parler de Tsama'). Glottolog 5.x files all these under mber1257 'Mbere-Mbamba' (ISO mdt), with dialects Ampiini, Lesia, Liengi, Nkomo, Ntaana, Obaa, Okumu, Ombamba-Congo, Osele, Oyuomi.
